gen-fs-synonym-fs-literata: Synonym draws its small curves wide open, with joins as slim as a pipe cleaner and no flaring at the stroke ends. Literata, a classic serif, is bookish by comparison, its thin and thick lines only gently different.
gen-fs-tanker-fs-karma: Tanker's most striking habit is turning every open curve inward, packing heavy letters tight with oversized lowercase. And Karma, a serif, does the opposite job, letting its terminals finish clear of the stem so text stays trustworthy and easy on the eye.
gen-fs-tanker-gf-graduate: Tanker is heavy and commanding, its curves turning inward and its letters crowded close with a lowercase that looms over the capitals. Graduate, a text serif, spreads out with generous white between letters, so a long passage would feel dignified and unhurried.
gen-fs-tanker-montserrat: Commanding and dense, Tanker closes up its curves and crowds its letters. Montserrat, a plain sans, does the opposite job well, with oversized e and a counters and lots of white leading into each curve, ideal for a handful of lines.
gen-fs-teko-fs-bespoke-sans: Bent steel, bolted tight. Teko's strokes never swell or thin, like cable shaped into letters, while Bespoke Sans lets its curve ends stand well clear of the stem, sharp and refined.
gen-fs-teko-fs-karma: Teko sets tightly packed letters in strokes like bent steel rod, with no hairlines and no shadows anywhere. Karma, a classic serif, handles the quieter work with moderate contrast.
gen-fs-teko-gf-graduate: Confident from the first glance, Teko packs its steel-rod strokes together with almost no gaps, while Graduate, a serif, spaces its letters out generously. Bold meets bookish here, tight against loose, and neither backs down.
gen-fs-telma-fs-alpino: Alpino is cozy and casual, with tall bodies that make its ascenders look short and its curve endings kept well apart. Telma, flowing and pen-written with a wide-mouthed a, earns its keep big and brief.
gen-fs-telma-fs-familjen-grotesk: Telma writes in flowing, pen-made letters with graceful weight changes. Familjen Grotesk, a sans-serif, brings lively bowls left open on one side, made for short stretches of reading.
gen-fs-telma-fs-hoover: Hoover is a robust text serif with compressed ascenders and a generous opening into the e. Next to Telma's flowing, pen-written script, a longer passage would read as refined and sturdy, never fussy.
